claim_ceiling: This P1 specification defines the versioned minimal WFF Core semantic contract, public/internal API boundary, declarative extension interface, compatibility postures, migration decisions, and structural conformance rules over the accepted P0 Core Candidate Map. It does not create a physical Core package, move runtime files, implement a generic plugin framework, prove exhaustive dynamic dependency closure, change P1-P4/PX behavior, authorize deletion, or establish v1.8 release readiness.

conformance_rules.statement: All nine P0 Core candidate contracts have one versioned P1 contract definition.
Every public operation references only declared public types and one declared contract.
Every current P0 capability has exactly one compatibility posture and at least one consumed contract.

The P1 public contract declares phase implementations, assurance, release/install tooling, fixtures, retained proof, and EKRI as forbidden Core dependency directions; physical conformance remains a P2/P4 proof obligation.
Extension registration is declarative and contains no executable loading surface.
Evidence/claim contracts preserve proof versus content-truth ownership.
Artifact identity remains storage-neutral and derived indexes remain non-authoritative.
Current public names/entrypoints/phase IDs/handoff/profile surfaces remain compatibility commitments through v1.8.
Physical extraction remains unauthorized until P2 registers change impact and proves forbidden dependency directions.
Contract conformance tests prove shape, reference closure, and dependency direction only; they do not certify business, architecture, implementation, validation, or release truth.

non_responsibilities: Does not generate requirements, architecture, implementation, validation, or brownfield content.
Does not hard-code executable implementation paths or import concrete extension modules.
contracts.summary: Represent external admission, internal continuation, route resolution, and stop outcomes without importing concrete capability implementations.
contracts.title: Lifecycle Route Contract

non_responsibilities: Does not decide product truth, architecture trade-offs, implementation content, or validation conclusions.
Does not require all phases to share one implementation or one phase-specific formal-state vocabulary.
contracts.summary: Define phase identity, truth owner, admission requirements, outputs, completion disposition, and allowed continuation.
contracts.title: Phase Contract

non_responsibilities: Does not replace upstream documents as sources of meaning.
Does not declare semantic sufficiency solely because required fields are present.
contracts.summary: Bind upstream authority, artifacts, evidence, unresolved items, allowed reliance, forbidden assumptions, and next-owner expectations.
contracts.title: Handoff Contract

non_responsibilities: Does not own document meaning, registry persistence, SQLite storage, reader projection, or file layout.
Does not require a single physical registry implementation.
contracts.summary: Define storage-neutral artifact identity, version, source authority, provenance, digest, and relationship bindings.
contracts.title: Artifact Identity Contract

non_responsibilities: Does not execute tests, Harnesses, reviews, or validators.
Does not convert a passing check into product, architecture, implementation, or production truth.
contracts.summary: Represent evidence identity, provenance, observation posture, scope, producer, integrity, and bounded supported claims.
contracts.title: Evidence Contract

non_responsibilities: Does not grant production approval, real UAT, owner sign-off, budget approval, or risk acceptance.
Does not define every phase-specific formal-state label as a global Core enum.
contracts.summary: Define claim-state envelopes, evidence ceilings, review-bound carryover, and weakest-evidence capping without replacing phase-specific state vocabularies.
contracts.title: Claim State Contract

non_responsibilities: Does not perform business, architecture, implementation, or review judgment in place of the responsible Agentic capability.
Does not make a schema, validator, template, or gate a hidden methodology.
contracts.summary: Preserve control ownership so Workflow orders work, Agentic owns semantic judgment, Templates guide depth, and Evidence/Gates prove or cap claims.
contracts.title: Workflow / Agentic / Templates / Evidence Boundary Contract

non_responsibilities: Does not load executable plugins, package extensions, or define installation mechanics.
Does not prove extension quality, standalone installability, or semantic correctness.
contracts.summary: Define a declarative capability descriptor and dependency rules so Core resolves contracts without dynamic plugin loading or concrete implementation imports.
contracts.title: Extension Registration Contract

non_responsibilities: Does not decide remediation content or silently rewrite upstream artifacts.
Does not turn PhaseX into a default phase after P4.
contracts.summary: Represent bounded remediation returns and PhaseX re-entry with owning phase, evidence, required action, minimum rerun boundary, and claim ceiling.
contracts.title: Return and Re-entry Contract

required_rules: Descriptor identity and contract-version range are mandatory.
Route keys are declarative and unique within one registry snapshot.
Phase extensions declare truth owner and public contracts consumed/produced.
Dependencies point from extension to Core public API or to explicitly declared non-Core peers; Core never imports implementations.
Ambiguous, unsupported-major, or unregistered descriptors fail closed.
Descriptor validation proves structure/reference closure only.

non_guarantees: Physical module paths are not stable public API.
Registry persistence and resolver algorithm are not extension API.
Internal validators do not own semantic truth.

surfaces.consumer_rule: Core implementation only; extensions consume public registration operations, not storage internals.
Core implementation only; algorithm and storage may change within compatible releases.
surfaces.purpose: Index route keys to descriptor identities.

surfaces.consumer_rule: May block malformed contracts but cannot decide semantic sufficiency or content truth.
Temporary/internal implementation; compatibility guarantees are declared in the public compatibility matrix.
surfaces.purpose: Resolve current public aliases during migration.

invariants.statement: Core may depend only on language/runtime primitives and its own public/internal contract types; capability, assurance, distribution, history, and EKRI dependencies point inward to Core.
Routing resolves registered declarative descriptors; descriptors do not contain executable loader hooks or require Core imports of implementations.
Ambiguous, unregistered, or unsupported routes do not fall back to guessed capabilities.
Route selection does not create requirements, architecture, implementation, validation, or brownfield truth.
Each phase extension retains its own content-truth owner; Core owns order and interfaces only.
Schema/field/reference checks establish structure, not semantic sufficiency.
Review-bound, provisional, unknown, conflict, and blocked states remain explicit across handoffs and claims.
Canonical artifacts own meaning; registries, indexes, readers, and projections do not replace them.
Missing upstream truth causes return, blocked, or explicit review-bound carryover rather than downstream invention.
Artifact identity and bindings do not depend on SQLite, directory layout, or one registry implementation.
Derived indexes and databases may accelerate lookup but never become canonical semantic authority.
Tests, runtime proof, reviews, validators, and gates prove or cap claims but do not author product/architecture/implementation truth.
Observed fact, inferred knowledge, unknown, and review-bound postures cannot be silently upgraded.
Evidence records identify scope, producer, provenance, and supported claims.
A claim cannot exceed the weakest missing mandatory evidence or authority boundary.
Core contracts do not imply real UAT, production approval, owner sign-off, budget approval, or production risk acceptance.
Core carries generic claim envelopes but phase-specific state labels and semantics remain owned by their capabilities.
Workflow owns route/phase order, required interfaces, stop/return paths, and evidence capture.
Agentic capability owners decide source truth, business semantics, architecture trade-offs, implementation meaning, and review judgments.
Templates and TVG guide questions/depth but do not decide answers or become hidden workflow control.
P1 defines the minimum declarative descriptor needed by current WFF capabilities; no dynamic plugin lifecycle, executable discovery, hot loading, or marketplace abstraction is introduced.
Extensions consume Core public contracts; Core does not consume extension implementation APIs.
Return/re-entry edges transfer control and evidence; they do not authorize cyclic package or module dependencies.

Current public skill names, entrypoints, phase IDs, handoff paths, and supported profile identifiers remain compatible throughout v1.8 unless an explicit issue, migration record, and final scenario evidence approve a change.

consequences: P1 creates no runtime directory move.
P2 must choose a physical home against this contract and EKRI impact evidence.
migration_decisions.decision: The versioned contract is the authority. Physical package/directory/language placement is deferred to P2 and may not weaken the contract.
migration_decisions.title: Core authority is semantic, not a preselected directory

consequences: Current three external routes and continuations can be expressed without Core importing implementations.
Installation and invocation remain outside the Core contract.
migration_decisions.decision: Extensions register identity, kind, route/phase bindings, consumed/produced contracts, truth owner, compatibility aliases, and failure policy. Core performs no dynamic executable discovery/loading.
migration_decisions.title: Use a declarative extension descriptor, not a generic plugin framework

consequences: P2/P3 must provide facades/adapters before moving implementations.
Removal is deferred to a future major contract version unless separately authorized.
migration_decisions.decision: Existing public skill names, entrypoints, P1-P4/PX identifiers, handoff paths, and supported profile identifiers cannot be removed during v1.8 absent a separate approved migration and final scenario proof.
migration_decisions.title: Preserve current compatibility surfaces for all of v1.8

consequences: Assurance depends inward on Core types.
A validator pass cannot create semantic truth.
migration_decisions.decision: Evidence identity, provenance, posture, claim ceilings, and generic claim-state envelopes are Core. Tests, Harnesses, validators, gates, P4 analysis, and Human Review remain outside Core.
migration_decisions.title: Core owns evidence and claim envelopes; assurance owns proof production and validation

consequences: The greenfield aggregate is split conceptually before physical extraction.
migration_decisions.decision: P1-P4/PX identities, admission/handoff/return interfaces, and order are Core contracts. Product, architecture, implementation, validation, and brownfield reasoning stay in their extensions.
migration_decisions.title: Phase spine is Core; phase implementations are extensions

consequences: Core cannot import SQLite or traceability implementation code.
P2 must define an adapter from current registry behavior to Core types.
migration_decisions.decision: Artifact references and bindings are Core. Registry persistence, SQLite projections, synchronization, and reader/index implementations remain non-Core extensions.
migration_decisions.title: Artifact identity is storage-neutral

consequences: Control-loop conformance is evaluated separately from package dependency cycles.
migration_decisions.decision: Core and package dependencies are acyclic and inward. P4 returns and PhaseX re-entry transfer control/evidence through packets and do not authorize cyclic imports.
migration_decisions.title: Dependency cycles are prohibited; return/re-entry is a control loop

consequences: Physical moves remain unauthorized until P2 dependency analysis.
P4 final package validation remains mandatory.
migration_decisions.decision: P1 defines forbidden directions and required audits but does not claim exhaustive import/subprocess/resource closure.
migration_decisions.title: Exhaustive dynamic dependency closure remains a P2/P4 obligation

public_api.claim: Public means stable semantic contract for WFF components, not a network API or public user plugin SDK.
public_api.dependency_rule: Capabilities, assurance, and distribution may consume this API. Core may not import those consumers.

public_operations.semantic_effect: Select one registered extension or fail closed; never infer content truth.
Record admission disposition while semantic sufficiency remains Agentic-owned.
public_operations.semantic_owner: Agentic phase owner constrained by Workflow order

public_operations.semantic_effect: Validate identity/reference completeness only; does not certify business or architecture sufficiency.
public_operations.semantic_owner: Workflow for structure; Agentic owner for sufficiency

public_operations.semantic_effect: Create a storage-neutral typed binding without changing document meaning.
Record bounded evidence provenance and posture; never upgrade inference to fact.
Cap supported state and claim text at the weakest mandatory evidence/authority boundary.
public_operations.semantic_owner: Evidence/Gates for ceiling; content owner for semantic claim

public_operations.semantic_effect: Prevent Workflow, Templates, or Evidence tooling from taking Agentic content-truth ownership.
Register declarative metadata only; no executable plugin discovery or loading.
Transfer control to the owning phase with evidence and rerun boundary; no cyclic code dependency.
public_operations.semantic_owner: Workflow for routing; target phase owner for remediation truth

fields.name: request_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity used to correlate one routing request with its resolution and later audit evidence.

fields.name: entry_kind
fields.semantic: Declares whether control enters from outside WFF, continues an accepted chain, returns for remediation, or re-enters from PhaseX.

fields.name: intent_key
fields.semantic: Normalized intent or route key resolved only against registered declarative extension metadata.

fields.name: source_refs
fields.semantic: Optional authoritative input artifacts that constrain route selection without becoming implementation paths.

public_types.semantic: A routing intent submitted at an external entry, accepted continuation, remediation return, or PhaseX re-entry boundary.

fields.name: request_id
fields.semantic: Identity of the route request whose resolution is recorded.

fields.name: disposition
fields.semantic: Fail-closed route outcome; only resolved permits dispatch to one registered extension.

fields.name: extension_id
fields.semantic: Registered extension selected when disposition is resolved; absent for all non-resolved outcomes.

fields.name: reason
fields.semantic: Reviewable explanation of the evidence, ambiguity, missing registration, or stop condition that produced the disposition.

public_types.semantic: The fail-closed result of resolving one route request against the current declarative extension registry snapshot.

fields.name: phase_id
fields.semantic: Stable phase identity used in routing, handoff, return, and compatibility records.

fields.name: phase_kind
fields.semantic: Distinguishes ordered mainline phases from sidecar assessment routes such as PhaseX.

fields.name: truth_owner
fields.semantic: Named capability role that owns semantic judgments and content truth produced within the phase.

fields.name: required_input_contracts
fields.semantic: Public contract envelopes that must be available before structural phase admission can be evaluated.

fields.name: allowed_next_phase_ids
fields.semantic: Declared continuation targets; omission does not authorize an undeclared or guessed next phase.

public_types.semantic: A phase identity and ownership declaration describing the contracts it consumes and the continuations it may permit.

fields.name: phase_id
fields.semantic: Phase whose admission decision is being recorded.

fields.name: disposition
fields.semantic: Bounded control outcome preserving normal admission, explicit review-bound progression, upstream return, or hard block.

fields.name: input_refs
fields.semantic: Authoritative input artifacts considered for admission and available for downstream review.

fields.name: semantic_judgment_owner
fields.semantic: Agentic owner responsible for deciding whether the admitted inputs are semantically sufficient.

fields.name: reason
fields.semantic: Evidence-linked rationale that distinguishes structural checks from the responsible semantic judgment.

public_types.semantic: A bounded phase-entry disposition that separates structural admission from Agentic semantic sufficiency judgment.

fields.name: artifact_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity independent of filename, directory location, registry backend, or rendered edition.

fields.name: artifact_type
fields.semantic: Declared semantic artifact class used to validate compatible bindings and handoff expectations.

fields.name: artifact_version
fields.semantic: Version or revision identity needed to prevent downstream consumers from binding to an unspecified artifact state.

fields.name: source_authority
fields.semantic: Document, phase owner, external authority, or accepted source that owns the artifact's meaning.

fields.name: location
fields.semantic: Resolvable storage location when available; location is not the artifact identity or semantic authority.

fields.name: content_digest
fields.semantic: Optional integrity digest binding the reference to exact content without making the digest a source of meaning.

public_types.semantic: A storage-neutral reference to one authoritative or derived artifact with explicit type, version, authority, location, and optional digest.

fields.name: binding_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity for one relationship so updates and audits do not depend on row order or storage implementation.

fields.name: subject_artifact_id
fields.semantic: Artifact whose relationship to another artifact, contract, evidence item, or authority is being declared.

fields.name: relation
fields.semantic: Typed relationship such as derives-from, satisfies, verifies, supersedes, or hands-off-to.

fields.name: object_ref
fields.semantic: Identity of the related artifact, evidence record, contract, or external authority.

fields.name: authority_ref
fields.semantic: Evidence or decision reference authorizing the relationship instead of allowing a derived index to invent it.

public_types.semantic: A typed relationship between artifact identities that preserves authority and provenance without replacing document meaning.

fields.name: evidence_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity for one evidence item across reports, gates, handoffs, and claim calculations.

fields.name: evidence_kind
fields.semantic: Classifies how the evidence was produced so consumers do not treat tests, reviews, and external authority as interchangeable.

fields.name: knowledge_state
fields.semantic: Preserves whether the evidence records observation, inference, absence of knowledge, or bounded review dependence.

fields.name: subject_refs
fields.semantic: Artifacts, contracts, behaviors, decisions, or claims whose bounded scope the evidence addresses.

fields.name: provenance
fields.semantic: Reviewable origin including producer, source/run identity, time or revision, and integrity reference where applicable.

public_types.semantic: A bounded evidence record identifying producer, provenance, knowledge posture, subject scope, and the claims it may support.

fields.name: claim_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity of the claim evaluation so state changes remain traceable across reruns.

fields.name: scope
fields.semantic: Exact artifact, phase, behavior, environment, or release surface to which the claim applies.

fields.name: requested_state
fields.semantic: State proposed by the responsible capability before evidence and authority ceilings are applied.

fields.name: supported_state
fields.semantic: Strongest state actually supported after mandatory evidence, unresolved items, and authority boundaries are evaluated.

fields.name: evidence_refs
fields.semantic: Evidence records used to support or cap the state; references do not create content truth.

fields.name: claim_ceiling
fields.semantic: Strongest plain-language claim permitted for the declared scope and current evidence/authority posture.

fields.name: ceiling_reason
fields.semantic: Weakest missing evidence, unresolved dependency, or absent authority that prevents a stronger claim.

public_types.semantic: A generic claim envelope recording requested and supported state, evidence bindings, and the weakest-evidence ceiling reason.

fields.name: item_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity for one unresolved statement, assumption, conflict, or missing proof across handoff and remediation cycles.

fields.name: status
fields.semantic: Explicit uncertainty/control posture that downstream must preserve rather than silently harden.

fields.name: owner
fields.semantic: Phase, role, external authority, or evidence producer responsible for resolving or accepting the item.

fields.name: verification_needed
fields.semantic: Concrete evidence, decision, review, or environment action needed before the item can change state.

fields.name: downstream_must_not_assume
fields.semantic: Forbidden downstream inference that prevents review-bound progression from becoming misleading certainty.

public_types.semantic: An explicit provisional, review-bound, blocked, unknown, or conflicting item carried without silently upgrading certainty.

fields.name: handoff_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity of the handoff decision and its evidence/artifact snapshot.

fields.name: from_phase_id
fields.semantic: Upstream phase or route that owns the committed outputs and declared limitations.

fields.name: to_phase_id
fields.semantic: Downstream phase or route permitted to consume the packet under its stated reliance limits.

fields.name: artifact_refs
fields.semantic: Authoritative and derived artifacts delivered by the upstream owner with stable identities.

fields.name: evidence_refs
fields.semantic: Evidence supporting the handoff decision and bounding what downstream may claim or rely on.

fields.name: unresolved_items
fields.semantic: Provisional, review-bound, blocked, unknown, or conflicting items that must remain visible downstream.

fields.name: decision
fields.semantic: Control disposition determining normal continuation, bounded progression, upstream return, or stop.

public_types.semantic: A cross-phase authority envelope describing artifacts, evidence, unresolved items, allowed progression, and return disposition.

fields.name: concern_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity of the engineering concern whose control and truth ownership are being separated.

fields.name: workflow_role
fields.semantic: Ordering, routing, input/output, handoff, stop/return, and repeatability responsibility assigned to Workflow.

fields.name: agentic_role
fields.semantic: Uncertainty, source interpretation, business/architecture/implementation meaning, and review judgment assigned to Agentic work.

fields.name: template_role
fields.semantic: Questions, depth prompts, output direction, and review concerns that guide without deciding the answer.

fields.name: evidence_role
fields.semantic: Proof production, defect exposure, blocking/routing, and claim-ceiling responsibility assigned to Evidence/Gates.

fields.name: forbidden_owner_transfer
fields.semantic: Explicit transfers that would turn Workflow, templates, validators, or gates into hidden content-truth owners.

public_types.semantic: A responsibility declaration preserving the distinct roles of Workflow, Agentic judgment, Templates/TVG, and Evidence/Gates.

fields.name: extension_id
fields.semantic: Stable declarative identity used by routing, compatibility, packaging, and dependency records without exposing a module path.

fields.name: extension_kind
fields.semantic: Classifies the extension's architectural role without granting truth ownership beyond its declared capability.

fields.name: core_contract_range
fields.semantic: Compatible public Core contract versions; an unsupported major version fails closed.

fields.name: route_keys
fields.semantic: Route-intent aliases resolved to this descriptor without embedding implementation paths.

fields.name: phase_ids
fields.semantic: Phase identities implemented or adapted by this extension.

fields.name: consumes_contracts
fields.semantic: Versioned Core public contracts consumed by the extension.

fields.name: produces_contracts
fields.semantic: Versioned public contract envelopes produced for downstream consumers.

fields.name: compatibility_aliases
fields.semantic: Existing public names or identifiers preserved by the extension during migration.

fields.name: truth_owner
fields.semantic: Capability or role that owns the semantic judgments and content truth produced by this extension.

fields.name: failure_policy
fields.semantic: Required behavior when registration, inputs, compatibility, or semantic authority are insufficient.

public_types.semantic: Declarative metadata for a phase, route adapter, support, assurance, or adaptation extension, with no executable loading semantics.

fields.name: packet_id
fields.semantic: Stable identity for one return or re-entry control transfer and its required remediation evidence.

fields.name: mode
fields.semantic: Distinguishes downstream defect remediation from an existing-system assessment re-entering the mainline.

fields.name: source_phase_id
fields.semantic: Phase or route that identified the gap, impact, or re-entry need and supplies the evidence.

fields.name: target_phase_id
fields.semantic: Owning phase responsible for the next semantic decision or remediation work.

fields.name: evidence_refs
fields.semantic: Evidence demonstrating why control must transfer and what the target owner must review.

fields.name: required_action
fields.semantic: Minimum concrete remediation, decision, or reconstruction action required before progression resumes.

fields.name: minimum_rerun_boundary
fields.semantic: Earliest phase or validation boundary that must be rerun after the required action completes.

fields.name: claim_ceiling
fields.semantic: Maximum claim allowed while the return or re-entry obligation remains unresolved.

public_types.semantic: A bounded control-transfer packet for remediation return or PhaseX re-entry, carrying owner, evidence, action, rerun boundary, and claim ceiling.

versioning_policy.v18_compatibility_rule: Keep current skill names, entrypoints, P1-P4/PX identifiers, handoff paths, and supported profiles throughout v1.8 unless explicit migration and final scenario proof approve a change.
